Source: A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with foul-smelling vaginal discharge.
She is sexually active and uses condoms.
A urine pregnancy test is negative.
She does not complain of any abdominal or pelvic pain but states she has some mild burning when urinating.
Some whitish discharge is noted from the urethra.
Her temperature is 97.6°F (36.4°C), blood pressure is 111/74 mmHg, pulse is 81/min, respirations are 12/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
Physical exam is notable for thick, white discharge from the cervix.
There is no cervical motion or adnexal tenderness or masses.
She states that it started 1 day ago and has not improved with hygiene products.
